title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a scratch sheet written on the verso of a typed EGA 0_IV draft, which shows through. It contains three loosely related jottings about positivity of algebraic cycles modulo numerical equivalence on a smooth projective variety X of dimension d.

(0) Top line: H^2(L^{⊗m} ⊗ K^{⊗(2m-1)}). This is probably an obstruction or vanishing group for a line bundle L and the canonical bundle K, for example on a surface. By Serre duality on a surface it is dual to H^0(L^{-m} ⊗ K^{2-2m}). It is isolated and its purpose cannot be determined.

(1) Numerical characterisation of ampleness. Grothendieck writes that D satisfies {D^d > 0 and D·C > 0 for every effective curve C > 0}. He marks this as equivalent to {D ∈ P_1^{+°} and α_{d-1}(D^{d-1}) ∈ P_1^+}. The likely notation is:
- A^i: codimension-i cycles modulo numerical equivalence (real coefficients); A_j: dimension-j cycles.
- P^+: the closed cone generated by effective classes.
- P^{+°}: the dual (numerically positive, 'nef') cone, i.e. classes meeting every effective cycle of complementary dimension non-negatively.
- α: a Lefschetz-type identification between complementary degrees, presumably via a fixed ample class ξ. The sub-arrow reads 'α D^{d-1} ξ ∈ P^{+°}_{d-1}'.
The point is to recast Nakai/Kleiman-type ampleness conditions as membership of D, and of the class of D^{d-1}, in positivity cones.

(2) He then isolates a QUESTION: α_{d-1}(P_{d-1}^{+°}) ⊂ P_1^+? In general, does the Lefschetz-type map send the dual-positive (nef) cone in one degree into the effective cone in the complementary degree? The boxed diagram states this for every i:
- P_i^{+°} ⊂ A^i →(α_i) A_{2d-i} ⊃ P^+_{2d-i};
- P^{+°}_{2d-i} ⊂ A^{2d-i} →(α_{d-i}) A_i ⊃ P_i^+;
- the refined form: int(P_i^{+°}) → P^+_{2d-i}?
The annotation P_i^{+°} = P^2_+ suggests that in the divisor/surface case the dual cone coincides with the positive cone, as Hodge index makes plausible.

(3) The final jotting 'c_i^?(E)' asks whether Chern classes of a positive (ample) vector bundle E lie in the positive cones P_i^+.

The whole page belongs to Grothendieck's programme on positivity cones in higher codimension and their compatibility with hard Lefschetz and Hodge-index type conjectures (the standard conjectures context of this archive box).
errors: As written, 'D^d>0 and D.C>0 for all effective curves C' is not a criterion for ampleness in dimension ≥3 (Nakai requires D^{dim V}·V>0 for all subvarieties V; Kleiman requires D in the interior of the nef cone). The claimed equivalence with the cone conditions is therefore at best heuristic. Its exact intended meaning depends on the undefined maps α_i.

The general inclusion asked in the Question (nef cone in codimension i mapped into the pseudoeffective cone) is false for the naive version 'nef ⇒ pseudoeffective' in higher codimension. Debarre–Ein–Lazarsfeld–Voisin (2011) found nef but non-pseudoeffective codimension-2 classes on abelian fourfolds. Whether Grothendieck's α (a Lefschetz-twisted map) avoids this is unclear from the page.
Indexing is inconsistent: α_i : A^i → A_{2d-i} versus α_{d-i} : A^{2d-i} → A_i. It mixes cohomological-degree and codimension conventions.

ideas.what: Positivity cones P_i^+ (effective) and P_i^{+°} (dual/numerically positive) in groups of cycles modulo numerical equivalence; ampleness expressed as membership of D in the interior of the dual cone
ideas.modern_name: Pseudoeffective and nef cones; Kleiman's ampleness criterion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kleiman (Annals 1966, 'Toward a numerical theory of ampleness'), building on Nakai–Moishezon
ideas.where_published: Possibly remarks in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969); Kleiman's work was done under Grothendieck's influence

ideas.what: Question whether the Lefschetz-type map sends the (interior of the) nef cone in degree i into the effective cone in the complementary degree
ideas.modern_name: Positivity of the Lefschetz isomorphism / 'nef implies pseudoeffective' in higher codimension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Question discussed by Fulton–Lazarsfeld school; counterexamples by Debarre–Ein–Lazarsfeld–Voisin (2011)

ideas.what: Positivity of Chern classes c_i(E) of ample vector bundles in the cones P_i^+
ideas.modern_name: Positivity of Chern classes of ample bundles

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly formulates, around 1965–71, a question on whether a Lefschetz-type map α_i sends nef classes (interior of the dual positive cone) in codimension i into the effective/pseudoeffective cone in the complementary degree, for all i. This is a precursor of the higher-codimension 'nef vs pseudoeffective' problem resolved negatively by DELV only in 2011. The Lefschetz-twisted version may differ from the naive one and seems not to have been examined as such.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives historical priority context for the positivity-of-cycles programme. The Lefschetz-twisted inclusion (as opposed to the identity inclusion) is a natural variant that remains of interest on abelian varieties and hyperkähler manifolds.

missed.claim: On a single sheet the page links positivity of Chern classes of positive bundles (c_i(E)) with the cone/Lefschetz question. This is the same link Bloch–Gieseker exploited in 1971 when they used hard Lefschetz to prove positivity of Chern classes of ample bundles.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it suggests Grothendieck saw Chern-class positivity as an instance of Lefschetz-compatible cone positivity.

deep.surprise_reason: These are fragmentary scratch notes, but they record an explicit general question on Lefschetz maps and positivity cones in all codimensions, together with Chern-class positivity. Both later became research themes (Bloch–Gieseker, Fulton–Lazarsfeld, DELV). The general circle of ideas is known to stem from Grothendieck/Kleiman, so this is a notable but not startling unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: 'D [-≠-]' is likely 'D' with a struck-out superscript; the bracket encloses the system {D^d>0, D.C>0 si C>0}.
The arrow under 'D ∈ P_1^{+°}' points to 'α D^{d-1} ξ ∈ P^{+°}_{d-1}' (with ξ an ample class); the small marginal note reads something like 'hyp de vie'/'hyp ⇒ vrai' and is uncertain.
In 'α_{d-1}D^{d-1} ∈ P_1^+' the subscript d-1 sits under α.
The line 'Question' is underlined 'Question' in the original.
In the boxed diagram the targets are A_{2d-i} ⊃ P^+_{2d-i} (the struck letter before 2d-i is a correction), and in the second row P^{+°}_{2d-i}.
